title: In 2016, Florida’s living shorelines withstood Hurricane Matthew’s 90 mph winds intact
summary_full: A living shoreline project in New Smyrna Beach largely survived Hurricane Matthew's severe winds. This natural approach used vegetation and sand to stabilize the coast effectively. Conventional hardened structures nearby experienced significant damage and erosion during the storm. The project demonstrated how natural defenses can withstand powerful hurricane conditions. This resilience offers a promising model for future coastal protection strategies.
